turns.doctor_question: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. It is nice to meet you; what brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response:
Nice to meet you, Dr. Smith. Well, I came in because I've been having this issue at work lately. I supervise a retail floor, and... when I try to explain the inventory numbers or go over the weekend schedule with my team, my words just start jumping all over the place. 

I'll be trying to talk about the delivery trucks, and then somehow I'm suddenly talking about Thursdays, or the church grill, or the tone of voice my boss was using earlier. It just comes out that way. And people... they just look at me like they can't follow what I'm saying at all. It's making it really hard to do my job, so I figured I needed to get it checked out.

symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient describes their words jumping between unrelated topics (trucks, Thursdays, church grill) and others being unable to follow what they are saying, which is indicative of disorganized thinking and speech (derailment/loose associations).
